section_summary: This section documents proceedings, political developments, and debates in the Imperial Japanese Diet between mid-1932 and early 1934, spanning the 62nd through the 65th sessions. Key topics include government policy toward the recognition and development of Manchoukuo, budget debates balancing agrarian relief against expanding army and navy appropriations, and controversies surrounding military involvement in domestic politics. The section also highlights diplomatic addresses by Foreign Ministers Yasuya Uchida and Koki Hirota, as well as an unexpected resurgence of Diet assertiveness in early 1934 challenging the military over international crisis rhetoric and naval treaty ratios.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Despatch No. 1746 from China concerning Count Uchida's Diet speech on the recognition of Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: This document file note cross-references Despatch No. 1746 dated September 10, 1932, originally filed under 893.00 P.R./60. It concerns Foreign Minister Count Uchida's address before the Imperial Diet regarding the recognition and establishment of the new state of Manchuria.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Speech by Count Uchida Before the Diet on Recognition of Manchuria

subfiles.about: Extract of a Tokyo Embassy report on the accomplishments of the 62nd extraordinary Diet session, Viscount Saito's speeches, and General Araki's remarks.
subfiles.summary: The report reviews the legislative results of the June 1932 extraordinary session of the Diet, including three budget bills and nineteen government measures. Premier Viscount Saito addressed parliament both as Premier and Foreign Minister, eventually regaining public confidence. War Minister General Sadao Araki apologized for military cadet involvement in the May 15 assassination of Premier Inukai and defended his retention of office.
subfiles.title: Despatch Extract: Accomplishments of the 62nd Extraordinary Diet Session

subfiles.about: Diplomatic analysis refuting Foreign Minister Count Uchida's Diet address regarding the creation of Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: The text provides a sharp critique of Foreign Minister Count Uchida's speech of August 1932 before the Japanese Diet, contrasting it with Secretary Stimson's pronouncement. It characterizes Japanese claims of spontaneous Manchurian independence as a deliberate distortion of facts. The report stresses that the new regime was created and maintained strictly by Japanese military power.
subfiles.title: Despatch Extract: Critique of Foreign Minister Uchida's Diet Speech on Manchuria

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 145 on the proceedings of the 63rd extraordinary Diet session.
subfiles.summary: This document file note indexes Despatch No. 145 (Political Report No. 58) dated October 4, 1932, from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew. It records the extraordinary session of the Imperial Japanese Diet held from August 22 to September 3, 1932, during which sixteen bills were passed.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Despatch No. 145 on the 63rd Extraordinary Diet Session

subfiles.about: Report section on the 63rd extraordinary Diet session detailing Seiyukai opposition, debates on rice control, and enacted legislation.
subfiles.summary: The report analyzes the extraordinary Diet session convened from August 22 to September 3, 1932. The Seiyukai majority in the Lower House attempted to amend the Rice Control Bill to inflate crop prices, drawing severe criticism from the House of Peers and the press until the government measure was largely restored. An Agrarian Debt Adjustment Bill was shelved after inter-house disagreement, but sixteen other measures, including budget deficit coverage and cooperative society regulations, were enacted.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 145 (Extract): Course of Legislation in the 63rd Extraordinary Diet Session

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 231 regarding the convening and opening of the 64th Diet session.
subfiles.summary: This document file note indexes Despatch No. 231 (Political Report No. 61) dated January 4, 1933. It notes that the 64th session of the Diet convened on December 24, 1932, and was formally opened by the Emperor on December 26.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Despatch No. 231 on Opening of the 64th Diet Session

subfiles.about: Extract detailing the formal opening of the 64th Diet session and the party strength in the House of Representatives.
subfiles.summary: This extract from Political Report No. 61 reports the convening and imperial opening of the 64th Diet session in late December 1932. It records the party representation in the Lower House, where the Seiyukai held 298 seats, the Minseito 116, and Kokumin Domei 33. The Diet immediately entered its New Year recess until January 20, 1933.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 231 (Extract): Opening and Party Alignment of the 64th Diet Session

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 278 on the reconvening of the 64th Diet session in January 1933.
subfiles.summary: This document file note records Despatch No. 278 (Political Report No. 62) dated February 2, 1933. It summarizes that the 64th Diet reconvened on January 20, 1933, after the holiday recess, with no major bills enacted prior to month's end.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Despatch No. 278 on the Reconvening of the 64th Diet Session

subfiles.about: Extract reviewing legislative proceedings during January 1933, including the fiscal year 1933-34 budget and electoral reform.
subfiles.summary: The extract discusses the reassembly of the 64th Diet on January 20, 1933, centering on the fiscal year 1933-34 budget and critical questioning of army and navy allocations. The Home Affairs Department introduced a contested Electoral Law revision to transfer campaign expenditures to the government. The Ministry of Finance prepared roughly a dozen bills, highlighted by an Exchange Control Bill.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 278 (Extract): Proceedings of the 64th Diet Session in January 1933

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 314 on the subdued Diet proceedings during February 1933.
subfiles.summary: This document file note indexes Political Report No. 63 (Despatch No. 314) dated March 1933. It notes that the Diet met in regular session throughout February 1933 without heated debates or significant constructive legislation.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Despatch on Diet Proceedings During February 1933

subfiles.about: Extract reporting on mild Diet debates, budget approvals, exchange control legislation, and Rashin harbor development in February 1933.
subfiles.summary: The report describes the peaceful proceedings of the Diet during February 1933, where legislators avoided criticizing military appropriations. The Lower House passed the 1933-34 budget and an Exchange Control Law giving sweeping authority to the Minister of Finance. A budget appropriation for constructing a harbor at Rashin, Korea, encountered questions regarding reports of seasonal ice.
subfiles.title: Despatch (Extract): Course of Legislation in the Diet During February 1933

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 348 on the conclusion of the 64th Diet session in March 1933.
subfiles.summary: This document file note indexes Despatch No. 348 (Political Report No. 64) dated April 1, 1933. It reports that the 64th session of the Diet adjourned on March 25, 1933, having enacted twelve budget-related measures.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Despatch No. 348 on the Close of the 64th Diet Session

subfiles.about: Report on political inertia, cabinet stability under Premier Saito, and enacted legislation at the close of the 64th Diet session.
subfiles.summary: The report characterizes the 64th Diet session as quiet and passive, attributing parliamentary restraint to fear of military and reactionary extremists. Despite rumors of resignation and health challenges, Premier Saito and Finance Minister Takahashi chose to remain in office to preserve political equilibrium. Legislative achievements included twelve budget bills, disaster relief for the Northern Honshu earthquake and tsunami, and an art preservation law motivated by the Boston Museum of Fine Arts acquiring the Kibi scroll.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 348 (Extract): Internal Politics and Legislation at the Close of the 64th Diet Session

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting that Foreign Minister Hirota's Diet address was transmitted to the Japanese Embassy in Washington.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew notifies the Secretary of State that Foreign Minister Koki Hirota addressed the Diet on January 23, 1934. The text was cabled directly to the Japanese Embassy in Washington, which would supply official copies to the State Department.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 14 from Tokyo Regarding Foreign Minister Hirota's Diet Address

subfiles.about: Memorandum transmitting and highlighting key sections of Foreign Minister Hirota's January 23, 1934 Diet address.
subfiles.summary: Stanley K. Hornbeck of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs submits a marked copy of Foreign Minister Koki Hirota's Diet speech to Secretary of State Cordell Hull and Under Secretary William Phillips. Portions considered of primary interest to American diplomacy were underlined in red for executive review.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum Forwarding Foreign Minister Hirota's Diet Address
subfiles.to: Secretary of State (Cordell Hull) and Under Secretary (William Phillips)

subfiles.about: Full text of Foreign Minister Hirota's address before the Diet outlining Japan's foreign policy and international relations.
subfiles.summary: Foreign Minister Hirota explains Japan's withdrawal from the League of Nations and reaffirms adherence to the Imperial Rescript promoting East Asian peace. He praises Manchoukuo's administrative consolidation and its impending transition to a monarchical regime under Pu Yi. Addressing relations with China, the Soviet Union, the United States, and Great Britain, Hirota advocates conciliation and diplomatic adjustment while expressing concern over worldwide trade barriers.
subfiles.title: Text of the Address of Foreign Minister Koki Hirota Before the Imperial Diet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 636 on the convening and formal opening of the 65th Diet session.
subfiles.summary: This document file note indexes Despatch No. 636 (Political Report No. 73) dated January 9, 1934. It notes that the 65th Diet convened on December 23, 1933, completed imperial opening ceremonies, and adjourned until January 22, 1934.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Despatch No. 636 on the Opening of the 65th Diet Session

subfiles.about: Extract analyzing the opening of the 65th Diet session, dissolution rumors, and anticipated political and economic controversies.
subfiles.summary: The extract discusses the opening ceremonies of the 65th Diet and discounts rumors of an early parliamentary dissolution. Political leaders anticipated confronting major challenges after the recess, including agrarian relief, trade controls, budget appropriations, and civilian-military sentencing disparities from the May 15 incident trials. Attention is also drawn to demands for peerage reform following gambling scandals among titled aristocrats.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 636 (Extract): Opening of the 65th Diet and Anticipated Legislative Issues

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum analyzing Tokyo Despatch No. 673 and attached clippings on parliamentary attacks on the military.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum summarizes Ambassador Grew's report on the 65th Diet session, emphasizing the unexpected vigor of parliamentary opposition to the military. It reviews press clippings concerning naval disarmament, public skepticism over the promoted 1935-36 international crisis, and proposed wheat anti-dumping legislation. It also assesses Kenkichi Yoshizawa's foreign policy speech and international reactions to Foreign Minister Hirota's diplomatic stance.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 673

subfiles.about: Report on the reconvened 65th Diet session, highlighting party cooperation in challenging the military over budgets and crisis rhetoric.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports an extraordinary shift in parliamentary behavior as Seiyukai and Minseito legislators launched coordinated attacks on military dominance upon reconvening in January 1934. Interpellators assailed disproportionate defense spending, cuts to agricultural relief, and military warnings of an impending 1935-36 crisis. Navy Minister Osumi defended naval policy and warned the Minseito regarding London Naval Treaty responsibility, while Finance Minister Takahashi defended currency management and postponed tax increases.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 673: Resurgence of Parliamentary Assertiveness and Attacks on the Military in the 65th Diet

subfiles.about: Collection of newspaper clippings and editorial translations from the Japanese press covering Diet debates on defense, finance, and trade.
subfiles.summary: This enclosure compiles English-language newspaper clippings and vernacular editorial translations from the Japan Advertiser, Asahi, and Hochi published between January 26 and 31, 1934. The articles cover parliamentary clashes over military discipline, defense spending, naval treaty ratios, and public fatigue with crisis agitation. Additional clippings report on Finance Minister Takahashi's opposition to premature yen devaluation, Ministry of Agriculture plans for wheat import restrictions, and commentary on parliamentary revival.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 673: Newspaper Clippings on Diet Proceedings
